content.user_title: Refactor Codebases with Clean Code Guidance
content.value_statement: Legacy code slows feature work and raises maintenance risk. This skill guides structured refactoring, clean code analysis, tests, and reviewable cleanup steps.
actual_capabilities: Identify code smells, SOLID violations, and performance risks in existing code.
Create prioritized cleanup plans with immediate fixes and larger refactor steps.
Suggest method extraction, class decomposition, dependency inversion, and pattern-based improvements.
Plan test coverage, regression checks, and before-and-after quality comparisons.
Guide migration steps when refactoring changes interfaces or dependencies.
limitations: Requires enough source context to judge coupling, tests, and business rules.
Does not replace project-specific test suites or human code review.
Broad architecture changes still need team approval and rollout planning.
Examples are educational and must be adapted to the target codebase.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Legacy Service
use_cases.description: Find high-impact refactor targets, split tangled responsibilities, and plan tests before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Feature Work
use_cases.description: Reduce duplication and coupling before adding new behavior to a risky module.

use_cases.title: Standardize Code Quality Reviews
use_cases.description: Use consistent clean code criteria, metrics, and verification steps across pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Find Cleanup Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for code smells, duplication, unclear names, and simple cleanup opportunities. Return a prioritized plan with risks and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a risky change
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this code before refactoring. Identify responsibilities, coupling, likely regressions, and the smallest safe sequence of changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply SOLID Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this component for SOLID violations. Recommend specific abstractions, dependency boundaries, and test coverage needed before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Migration Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for this refactor. Include compatibility needs, rollout steps, verification checks, and how to compare quality before and after.

output_examples.input: A long order-processing module mixes validation, database access, notifications, and logging.
output: Priority one: separate validation and persistence because they create the highest regression risk.
Refactor sequence: add characterization tests, extract validator, extract repository, then isolate notifications.
Verification: run order workflow tests and compare error handling before and after the cleanup.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce technical debt before adding a new checkout feature.
output: Recommended scope: remove duplication in pricing rules and add tests for current edge cases.
Defer broad architecture changes until the feature risk is better understood.
Expected impact: lower change risk and clearer ownership of pricing behavior.

best_practices: Define the refactor scope and success criteria before editing code.
Use tests and targeted regression checks to protect existing behavior.
Prefer small, reviewable changes with clear before-and-after rationale.
anti_patterns: Starting a broad rewrite without agreement on scope or rollback options.
Refactoring behavior without tests or another reliable verification method.
Adding design patterns that do not reduce real complexity or coupling.

faq.question: Can this skill edit code directly?
faq.answer: Yes, when used in an agent that has file editing access. It should keep changes small and verified.

faq.question: Does it support large codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to prioritize cleanup work and avoid unbounded rewrites.

faq.question: Will it choose a design pattern automatically?
faq.answer: It can recommend patterns, but the pattern should solve a clear coupling or maintainability problem.

faq.question: How should teams verify refactors?
faq.answer: Run existing tests, add focused regression tests, and compare behavior before and after each step.

faq.question: Is this only for object-oriented code?
faq.answer: No. The guidance covers general code smells, testing, performance, and modular design across languages.

faq.question: Can it help with migration planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline compatibility needs, rollout steps, and checks for interface changes.
